message.content: {"bid_amount":46,"public_message":"$46.","private_thought":"Min-raise. p4 caps at $74 cash and has no spare mortgage cushion except dark blues (houses must be sold first). Kentucky under $110 is free money if I later mortgage it, and winning denies p4 a $110 emergency mortgage that would save BW houses. If they hit $74 I take it at $75. Do not go above $110. Keep cash for PA Ave, jail exit, and a hit. Don't mortgage greens, Ventnor, or CT."}
message.reasoning:
I need to decide on an auction bid for Kentucky Avenue.

I'm in jail with $1179 and no monopolies. The auction is at $45, with p4 holding only $74 cash. I'll bid $46 to win.

I'll bid $46 to win under the $110 mortgage value. I need to keep about $320 for Pacific Avenue and other expenses. I won't mortgage my greens or Connecticut.

I'm reconsidering the $46 bid. If I drop out, p4 gets Kentucky for $45 and still has $29 cash. That isn't draining them much. I could bid higher to force them to spend more of their $74. But the rent on Kentucky is only $18, so it may not be worth that much.

Mortgaging Kentucky immediately after purchase would net $37 profit. That makes the bid more attractive. I'm weighing whether to mortgage it or keep it as a rent chip.

Mortgaging won't block p3 from buying reds. I'll keep bidding to drain p4's $74 cash, then claim Kentucky cheap if they drop out.

I'm comparing two paths: bidding up to $75 and mortgaging Kentucky for a $35 profit, or dropping at $74 and leaving p4 with no cash. I'm also calculating p4's rent threat from their dark-blue properties.

Draining p4 to zero cash is the better path. They cannot build more houses on their dark-blue properties with only $74, so any rent forces them to sell houses and degrades their monopoly. A useless Kentucky purchase would leave them cash-broke and unable to threaten rent.

I'm now calculating the exact rent thresholds. With $74 cash, p4 can pay small rents on Mediterranean, Connecticut, and Ventnor without selling houses. At zero cash, any rent forces them to sell a house. They must sell evenly across their two dark-blue properties.

Selling one Boardwalk house would slash p4's rent from $600 to $200. That is a major threat reduction. I will keep bidding until p4 hits their $74 cap, then raise to $75 if they match.

I'm now weighing a $73 bid. If p4 matches at $74, I can drop and leave them cash-broke. If they bid $75, I win under the $110 mortgage value for a $35 profit. I'll own Kentucky mortgaged, which blocks p3 from getting a cheap third red, though the red set can't complete anyway without a trade.

The $35 mortgage profit is minor compared to the strategic value of degrading p4's dark-blue threat. Boardwalk with two houses at $600 rent is the real danger; reducing it to $200 by forcing a house sale is survival. I also need cash for the $50 jail fee on my next turn.

$1179 is enough to buy Pennsylvania Avenue for $320 even after a $75 Kentucky bid. I'm now comparing the remaining threats. p4's dark blues are static because they cannot build with only $74 cash. p3's pink set could still grow since they have $97 and house costs are $100. p1's orange properties are heavily built but mortgaged with only $15 cash, so they pose no threat.

p3's pink set is the active threat. p4 cannot build with only $74 cash, so they cannot escalate their dark-blue monopoly.

If p4 mortgages Kentucky for $110 after buying it, they would have $110 cash. That still does not let them build houses, but it would let them pay some rents without selling.

I'm now unsure whether p4 will mortgage Kentucky immediately. Their robotic $1 increments suggest a simple bot that might not optimize, leaving them cash-broke and vulnerable. If they are smart, they would mortgage and keep roughly $110, but still cannot build. The key question is whether any cash level actually forces house sales.

I realized the drain-to-zero plan has a fatal flaw. If p4 owns Kentucky unmortgaged, they can mortgage it for $110 to pay rent instead of selling houses. They would still have roughly $110 cash and could build again. The threat reduction is not guaranteed.

I will bid to win Kentucky myself. This prevents p4 from using it as an emergency mortgage cushion, leaving them with no extra cash buffer and forcing house sales on their dark-blue properties.

I'm now calculating the exact orange-rent threat. p4's Tennessee with three houses could hit $750, which would bankrupt them if they have no mortgageable property left. I need to verify the standard orange-rent values before finalizing my bid.

I've verified the exact orange-rent schedule. St. James Place with three houses pays $750, Tennessee with three houses pays $750, and New York with three houses pays $800. These are the standard base, one-house, two-house, three-house, four-house, and hotel values.

p1's orange monopoly is intact. St. James Place, Tennessee, and New York are all owned and unmortgaged with houses built. The three-house Tennessee rent is $550. That is a major threat to p4 with only $74 cash.

p3's pink set is now fully mapped. St. Charles Place with two houses pays $200, States Street with three houses pays $550, and Virginia Avenue with three houses pays $600.

p4 is currently on Illinois Avenue after paying the $20 rent. Their next roll will land them on several high-rent spaces including Ventnor Avenue, Water Works, and Pacific Avenue.

With only $74 cash and no mortgageable property to fall back on, p4 cannot afford these upcoming rents without selling houses.

I will bid $46 to win the auction. I am not jumping straight to $75 because p4 may drop out at that point. I will keep raising by one dollar until they match or fold.

I confirmed that p4 cannot mortgage mid-auction, so their maximum bid is fixed at $74. I will raise to $46 now and then bid $75 on the next turn if they match. I am also weighing whether dropping out is ever a viable option.
